transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I've been dealing with really exhausting mood swings over the last several months. Sometimes I feel this intense, overflowing energy and can't stop moving, but then I crash into feeling completely empty, sad, and unmotivated. It's just getting too hard to manage on my own.
During your high or low moods, have you ever heard or seen things other people couldn't, or had beliefs that others said were not true?

Yes, I actually have, but only during those times when my energy and mood were extremely high. I've heard voices and felt convinced that I had special powers or that people were watching me, but that never happens when I'm in my low periods. It only occurs when I'm feeling that intense rush.
Have you ever had hallucinations or delusional beliefs when your mood was not unusually high or low, even for a day or two?
No, absolutely not. Those experiences only happen when I'm feeling extremely high, energetic, and active. When my mood is normal or stable, those voices and strange beliefs completely go away.

Have you ever had a period of at least one week where your mood was so high or irritable and your energy was so increased that you needed much less sleep, felt unusually grand, and it caused major problems or led to hospitalization?

Yes, I absolutely had a period like that which lasted for about four months. During that time, my mood was incredibly elevated and irritable, my energy was overflowing, and I truly believed I had special powers. It caused a lot of problems, especially when I went on reckless, unrestrained buying sprees that I'm still trying to recover from.

The patient describes a 4-month period of elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, grandiosity, reckless spending, and hallucinations/delusional beliefs that were confined to the mood episode and absent when mood was normal. That makes Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features the best fit and makes Bipolar I Disorder without psychotic features unlikely.

inference_history.note: Previously the candidates were broader mood disorders including Bipolar I/II and depressive disorders. The new information shows psychotic symptoms (voices, grandiose/paranoid beliefs) occur only during periods of markedly elevated mood/energy, which makes primary psychotic disorders and depressive disorders less likely. This pattern supports a bipolar-spectrum illness with psychotic features, so Bipolar II is less likely because psychosis implies mania rather than hypomania, and Major Depressive Disorder/Persistent Depressive Disorder are no longer good fits. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) remains on the list only if psychotic symptoms also occur outside mood episodes, which has not been established yet. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features is the leading candidate, with Bipolar I Disorder and Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) still in the differential pending clarification of whether there are any psychotic periods without mood symptoms.
